messages.content: The client finally confirmed the Cleveland details. The sessions are at the hospital campus near University Circle, Tuesday starts at 9:00, Wednesday is a full onsite day, and Thursday closeout is supposed to end by 2:00. Can you compare the realistic flight and hotel combinations now and give me an approval-ready plan?

Yes. I can narrow this a lot now. I am treating the hospital campus location as the anchor, with no rental car unless the client tells us otherwise. The only missing items I would still flag are the exact building entrance, any client hotel rate code, and whether your booking has to go through Concur after approval. For flights, the clean outbound is the Monday late-morning nonstop ATL to CLE, arriving early afternoon. For the return, there are two useful nonstops: midafternoon gets you home earlier but is tight after a 2:00 closeout; early evening gives a safer buffer.
Booking will be through Concur after my manager approves it. No rate code yet. What are the return tradeoffs exactly?

Here is the clean comparison. Option 1: Monday late-morning nonstop out, Thursday midafternoon nonstop back. This is the earliest-home option, but after a 2:00 closeout you would need the meeting to end on time, get out quickly, and have a smooth rideshare to the airport. It works only if the client is disciplined about ending. Option 2: same Monday outbound, Thursday early-evening nonstop back. This adds a couple of hours in Cleveland but gives room if the closeout runs 20 to 45 minutes long or rideshare timing is uneven. Option 3: one-stop return. It is still only modestly cheaper and adds connection risk on a short work trip, so I would not put it forward unless there is a budget push.
Use the early-evening return unless the hotel location makes the midafternoon one genuinely workable. Can you put the hotel choices next to that?

The hotel choice actually points toward keeping the early-evening return. Campus-adjacent option: Courtyard Cleveland University Circle, roughly $230s before tax on the flexible rate, strong guest ratings, close to the hospital campus, on-site Bistro/cafe, nearby dinner options, but breakfast is paid. Downtown option: Hampton Inn or similar downtown property, roughly $185 to $205 before tax, breakfast included, decent ratings, more downtown restaurants, but rideshare-dependent for every hospital-campus morning. Airport-area option: cheaper, roughly $135 to $155 before tax and often includes breakfast, but it makes both onsite days more complicated with longer rideshares and less control over traffic.
Which campus hotel are you assuming? The earlier list had a few around University Circle.

I am using Courtyard Cleveland University Circle as the approval candidate. It lines up best with University Hospitals and Case Western rather than pushing you toward downtown or the airport. The paid breakfast is the main drawback, but the location saves time on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday mornings. I would verify the exact cancellation deadline on the booking page before purchase.
The address they sent is University Hospitals main campus, not Cleveland Clinic. Does that change anything?

Yes, that strengthens the case for the University Circle hotel. If it were Cleveland Clinic, I would compare the InterContinental properties more closely. For University Hospitals main campus, Courtyard University Circle is the cleaner commute. Downtown is still workable, but it turns a simple morning into a rideshare calculation.
I do not care if breakfast is paid if the mornings are easier. Is the campus property under $250 before tax and cancellable?

The current flexible quote I see is about $232 before taxes and fees for a king room, with cancellation allowed until shortly before arrival. I would not use a prepaid or nonrefundable version for this trip. Breakfast is not included, so I would plan on the hotel cafe or a nearby quick stop, roughly $12 to $18 depending on what you get.
Good. How should I explain not taking downtown with free breakfast?

I would frame it as operational rather than preference-based: downtown saves some room cost and includes breakfast, but it adds a rideshare commute for each hospital-campus morning, including the 9:00 Tuesday start. The campus hotel costs more and breakfast is paid, but it reduces timing risk and keeps the worksite logistics simpler.
And the airport hotel?

I would rule it out for the approval plan. The nightly savings look tempting, but the airport area creates the longest commute, more rideshare dependence, and the least flexibility if the onsite schedule changes. It only makes sense if your manager asks for the absolute cheapest acceptable option.
Okay. Put forward the Monday late-morning nonstop, Thursday early-evening nonstop, and Courtyard University Circle. Include no car and that the one-stop fares are not worth it.

That is the plan I would send for approval. Remaining items before booking: confirm the hotel rate is still cancellable in Concur, confirm the exact cancellation deadline, check whether the hotel can store luggage after Thursday checkout, and select seats once the flights are ticketed. I will also note no rental car because the hotel, campus, and airport can be handled by rideshare.
Please draft the approval blurb. Keep it concise.

Draft: Request approval for Cleveland client build sessions, Aug. 18 to Aug. 21. Recommended itinerary is a Monday late-morning nonstop ATL-CLE and a Thursday early-evening nonstop CLE-ATL. The early-evening return is preferred over the midafternoon return because Thursday closeout is scheduled to end at 2:00 and may run long. Recommended hotel is Courtyard Cleveland University Circle on a cancellable rate, currently under $250 before taxes, because it is close to the University Hospitals campus and reduces morning commute risk. Downtown and airport hotels were reviewed; downtown includes breakfast but adds rideshare-dependent mornings, and airport-area savings are offset by longer commutes. One-stop flights are only modestly cheaper and add avoidable connection risk. No rental car requested; rideshare is expected to be sufficient.
Add one line that the return gives buffer if the closeout slips a little.

Added. Final approval-ready version: Request approval for Cleveland client build sessions, Aug. 18 to Aug. 21. Recommended itinerary is a Monday late-morning nonstop ATL-CLE and a Thursday early-evening nonstop CLE-ATL. The later return provides a practical buffer if Thursday closeout slips past the expected 2:00 end time. Recommended hotel is Courtyard Cleveland University Circle on a cancellable rate, currently under $250 before taxes, because it is close to the University Hospitals campus and reduces morning commute risk. Downtown and airport hotels were reviewed; downtown includes breakfast but adds rideshare-dependent mornings, and airport-area savings are offset by longer commutes. Take the rear windows. A forward middle is not worth it. Also add a quiet-room request at the hotel if there is a field for it.

Got it. I have the flight itinerary ready to ticket: ATL to CLE Monday 10:45 a.m. to 12:26 p.m., nonstop; CLE to ATL Thursday 6:12 p.m. to 7:58 p.m., nonstop. Main Cabin fare is still within the approved estimate. Available seats are 23A outbound and 24A return. Proceed with ticketing?

Flights are ticketed. Confirmation CLE7M2. Seats selected: 23A ATL-CLE and 24A CLE-ATL. I saved the airfare receipt and fare rules to the Cleveland folder. Moving to the hotel now, but I will check the cancellation language before booking.

Hotel check: Courtyard Cleveland University Circle, king room, flexible rate, about $232 before taxes and fees. Cancellation is allowed until Aug. 16 at 11:59 p.m. hotel time. It is a card guarantee, not a prepaid rate. Breakfast is not included, but the Bistro opens early and there are several nearby dinner options. Good to book?
Yes, book that one. Quiet room away from the elevator if they let you request it.

Booked. Hotel confirmation CY-48176. I added the request: quiet room away from elevator, higher floor if available. The request is not guaranteed, but it is attached to the reservation. I also saved the cancellation policy showing the Aug. 16 deadline.
Add the rideshare note and put the confirmations where reimbursement can find them.

Done. The Cleveland folder now has the flight receipt, fare rules, seat assignments, hotel confirmation, hotel cancellation terms, and the no-rental-car note. Ground plan: rideshare CLE to hotel Monday, short rideshare or walk depending on the exact campus entrance Tuesday through Thursday, and rideshare back to CLE Thursday afternoon. Breakfast is not included, so I noted the hotel Bistro as the simple morning fallback and nearby restaurants for dinner.
Anything else I should check before travel week?

Only a few items: check in for the outbound when it opens on Sunday, reconfirm seats 23A and 24A, verify the client sends the exact building entrance, and ask the hotel at check-in about Thursday luggage storage. No rental car is on the itinerary, and all receipts are saved for reimbursement.

You would need to leave campus around 4:05, pick up your bag by about 4:20, be in a rideshare by 4:30, and hope to reach the airport around 5:00. For a 6:12 departure, that is too dependent on everything going smoothly.
